newsitem.title: USA: Ameristar starts proceedings against pair.
newsitem.headline: Ameristar starts proceedings against pair.

text.p: Ameristar Casinos Inc said Thursday it had started arbitration proceedings against Steven Rebeil and Dominic Magliarditi, former stockholders of Gem Gaming Inc.
Ameristar alleges the pair breached the merger agreement under which Gem was acquired by Ameristar last October.

Ameristar said that due to uncertainties related to the merger agreement, bank lenders have postponed completion of an increase in its credit facility to $175 million from $94.5 million. The credit deal had been scheduled to close this week.

Construction on The Reserve casino-hotel in Henderson, Nev., acquired under construction through the merger, will be delayed pending resolution of the uncertainties or the availability of alternative financing, Ameristar said.
Notwithstanding the arbitration proceedings and the delayed construction, the company said it believes it has adequate liquidity and capital resources to meet its obligations.
It also said the events will have no material impact on its existing casino properties.
In the absence of an enhanced credit facility or other financing, Ameristar said it would complete certain construction work in progress and delay other construction on The Reserve.
In the merger with Gem, Gem holders were to receive net proceeds, minus certain reductions, of a public offering of 7.5 million shares of Ameristar to be completed by June 1.

If the offering is not completed, the pact says Gem holders will get three-year 8.0 percent promissory notes in a principal amount equal to 7.5 million multiplied by the average closing price of Ameristar's stock during the last 10 trading days of May 1997, less the same reductions.
The agreement does not give the holders the right to select the form of consideration, Ameristar said.
Ameristar alleges that Rebeil and Magliarditi have wrongfully impeded the stock offering because they believe the promissory notes would yield a greater amount.
It said it is seeking damages and declaratory relief to establish the amount and terms of the merger consideration.
